## Design

All observations are synthetic. This experiment uses independent training,
calibration, and test cohorts, with the same target population within a scenario.
The shared linear model is fitted using training data only. Conformal calibration
uses absolute residuals separately in the control and investigational arms.
The nominal prediction coverage is 90% under the default configuration.

```{r}
knitr::kable(read.csv("outputs/conformal/repeated_configuration.csv"))
```

These cohorts are separate from the 240-patient efficacy trial. This comparison
isolates predictive calibration, not performance achievable from that trial alone.

## Calibration details from the individual run

```{r}
knitr::kable(read.csv("outputs/conformal/calibration_details.csv"), digits = 3)
```

## Repeated coverage and width

```{r}
knitr::kable(results[results$group %in% c("Overall", "Control", "Investigational"), ], digits = 4)
```

Monte Carlo uncertainty is computed across independent repetitions. Prediction
coverage concerns future individual outcomes; it is not confidence-interval coverage
for the mean treatment effect. Standard split conformal validity is marginal over
calibration and a future patient, within the calibrated arm.

## Biomarker diagnostics

```{r}
knitr::kable(results[grepl("Biomarker", results$group), ], digits = 4)
```

These strata were not separately calibrated. Their coverage is a diagnostic and
is not protected by the arm-specific guarantee. The nonlinear scenario also has
larger residual variance for patients with positive biomarker values.

## Individual prediction examples

```{r}
knitr::include_graphics("outputs/conformal/individual_prediction_intervals.png")
```

The plot shows the first 30 test patients, selected independently of outcomes.
Green intervals contain the observed outcome; red intervals miss it.

## Limitations and next steps

The first scenario matches the model assumptions; the second violates mean and
variance assumptions while preserving cohort exchangeability. This is not a
population-shift study. No superiority is assumed in advance. CRC for adverse-event
prediction remains a separate planned module. See docs/conformal-results-guide.md.
